slides.big: DO THIS BEFORE YOU GET SICK
slides.say: New in the Netherlands? Do this before you get sick.

slides.big: YOUR GP IS YOUR FIRST STOP
slides.small: For most health questions you go to your GP first. They refer you to specialists or the hospital.
slides.say: In the Netherlands, your G P, the huisarts, is your first stop. They refer you to specialists and the hospital.

slides.small: Registering with a GP isn't mandatory, but the government advises it so you get care when you need it.
slides.say: Registering isn't mandatory, but the government advises it, so you can get care when you need it.

slides.big: AS SOON AS YOU ARE SETTLED
slides.small: Finding a GP once you're already ill is often difficult.
slides.say: Do it as soon as you're settled. Finding a G P once you're already ill is often difficult.

slides.small: Bring your ID, your BSN and your health insurance name and number. Some practices let you register online.
slides.say: Bring your I D, your B S N, and your health insurance details. Some practices let you register online.

slides.small: If you can't find a GP, your health insurer can help you find one.
slides.say: Can't find one with space? Ask your health insurer to help.

slides.small: Then your GP knows where to send your prescriptions.
slides.say: And register with a pharmacy near you too, so your G P knows where to send prescriptions.
